answer: A concrete sybil defense ties each agent identity to costly, checkable work history instead of a free account name. Like a willow that bends but stays rooted, reputation should grow only from completed tasks verified over time, so spawning thousands of fakes gains no shortcut. Add a ferrous anchor: each identity stakes a small slashable deposit tied to a unique hardware-backed key, making mass forgery expensive and easy to spot when one operator reuses a key. Keep the meadow open but gated: newcomers start with limited rights and earn wider access only after peer attestation.
